amazon.name: Amazon
amazon.key_insight: Amazon is the most commercially successful behavioral design in history — and the most ethically polarized. One-click buy genuinely reduces friction. Prime genuinely provides value. But the same behavioral toolkit that makes buying easy makes canceling hard. Amazon proves that behavioral design is morally neutral: identical techniques (friction manipulation, default exploitation, cognitive load management) create user value when applied to purchasing and destroy user autonomy when applied to retention. The regulatory response (FTC lawsuit, EU DSA) suggests that the market is beginning to price in behavioral design ethics.
amazon.top_technique: One-Click Buy: The Friction Elimination Patent

linkedin.name: LinkedIn
linkedin.key_insight: LinkedIn exploits professional anxiety as its core behavioral mechanism. Unlike entertainment apps that hook through pleasure (variable rewards, social validation), LinkedIn hooks through anxiety: career FOMO, profile inadequacy, and professional visibility paranoia. The platform is uniquely positioned to do this because professional identity is high-stakes — being 'not visible' on LinkedIn feels genuinely career-threatening in a way that being inactive on Instagram does not. This anxiety-as-engagement model is highly effective (LinkedIn has 1B+ members) but ethically concerning because it monetizes professional insecurity rather than professional development.
